title: Polygon Plans Hard Fork to Seize $6.5 Million From Polymarket and Binance Hackers

content: Polygon has proposed a hard fork to recover millions of dollars lost in recent security breaches affecting Polymarket and Binance. The radical intervention aims to wipe funds from hacker wallets, though critics point out that it challenges the core immutability principle of Web3.

title: 58% of UK Adults Not Ready to Let AI Manage Their Money, Despite Widespread Use, FIS Research Finds
summary:
UK consumers are already using artificial intelligence (AI) for help with their money, but most are not ready to let it take control. They want firm spending limits, a guaranteed refund and a person who can step in before they will trust AI to act on their behalf. This is according to new research from global financial technology leader FIS®.
The 2026 FIS Consumer Pulse Survey of 2,000 UK adults found that 58% are not ready to hand their day-to-day money management to an AI assistant. Only 22% say they are ready, compared with 37% in the US. Despite this, many consumers are happy to use AI as a helper. More than half (58%) have turned to GenAI tools such as ChatGPT or Claude in the past 12 months for tasks like budgeting, answering a question about their account or choosing a financial product, and 64% expect to in the next 12 months.
Adoption is real, but letting go is not
UK consumers are already bringing AI into their financial lives. As well as general GenAI tools, 56% have used an AI assistant within their banking app for something to do with their money in the past year. But using AI to answer a question or plan a budget is different from letting it act. Half (51%) of UK adults have never heard of agentic banking, in which AI carries out banking tasks on a customer’s behalf.
Readiness to hand over day-to-day money management is low across every generation. Millennials (33%) are the most ready, followed by Gen Z (27%), Gen X (15%), adults aged 62 to 69 (8%) and those aged 70 and older (3%). Young UK adults are significantly less likely to indicate readiness to as their US counterparts, where 61% of Millennials and 58% of Gen Z say they are ready.
The findings come as UK banks and regulators begin testing AI that acts for customers. The Financial Conduct Authority’s (FCA) AI Live Testing service, whose second cohort began testing in April 2026, includes firms trialing agentic payments, and on 19 October 2026 the FCA published examples of good and poor practice for AI in financial services. As AI moves from pilot to product, consumers will help set the pace.
Kanv Pandit, Head of International Markets – Banking and Payments, at FIS said: “UK consumers aren’t rejecting AI, and most are already using it to help with their finances, but they aren’t ready to give up control. The message for banks is clear: start with the tasks people already welcome, like stopping a suspicious charge, let customers set the limits and be clear about who is accountable when something goes wrong. Banks that get this right will earn consumers’ trust to let AI do more on their behalf.”
Drawing the line on what AI can do
Comfort with AI depends on the task. UK adults are most comfortable with an AI assistant flagging or freezing a suspicious charge (56%), paying a recurring bill they have approved before (52%) and rounding up purchases into savings (51%). Comfort falls for sending money to another person or business (38%), opening a new savings or deposit account (35%) and applying for a loan or credit card (30%).
UK adults also want tight limits on spending. More than half (56%) would not let an AI assistant in their banking app spend or move any money without approving the transaction. Among those who would, 35% would cap it at £250 or less, and just 5% of all UK adults would allow more than £500 or set no limit.
Consumers are writing the terms for AI
UK consumers are clear about what it would take to trust AI with their money. 62% rank a guaranteed refund for any mistake among their top three conditions, higher than in the US (58%) and Singapore (57%), followed by a person who can review or override decisions (51%), and a strong security and fraud-protection track record (47%).
Among those not ready to hand over day-to-day money management, 64% say they want to stay in control of their own money, 50% don’t trust AI to get it right and 48% worry it could make costly mistakes.
Pandit added: “The UK is telling banks exactly what trustworthy AI looks like. Consumers want a refund if something goes wrong, a person who can step in and the freedom to set their own limits. Trust is the deciding factor for whether consumers let AI act on their behalf, and it has to be earned before AI acts, not repaired afterwards. That means building safeguards in from the start. FIS Orchestrated Intelligence is designed to do exactly that. It works within the limits customers set, explains its decisions and keeps a person in the loop so trust is assured before AI acts on anyone’s behalf. Banks that put trust first will be the ones consumers allow to do more.”

title: Half of UK Consumers Willing to Switch to Islamic Finance
summary:
Half of UK consumers (50%) have shared that they would be willing to switch from conventional banking to Islamic finance if it offered comparable services, according to new research published by Gatehouse Bank.
The Islamic finance industry is one of the fastest growing areas of financial services globally, predicted to grow to over US$4 trillion in assets by 2030, from a market of US$200 billion in 2003. This global growth opportunity is complemented by strong consumer demand in the UK, with Shariah-compliant products and services proving popular among consumers of all religions or of no religion.
The Bank’s new research follows two years after the publication of its Islamic and Ethical Finance Consumer Report, which examined perceptions, awareness and understanding of Islamic, ethical and green finance in the UK. Not only does the latest research show a continued willingness to switch but awareness of Islamic finance remains strong, with over two fifths (41%) of respondents stating that they have at least some knowledge of the industry.
The UK’s Islamic finance industry has been growing over recent years and is now home to approximately 20 institutions providing Islamic finance products, including five fully Shariah-compliant banks.
Motivating factors
When asked what would motivate them to choose Islamic finance, respondents cited alignment with their value system and beliefs (19%) and that providers are trustworthy and transparent (18%) as the most important factors. This rises considerably among Muslim consumers, with over a third (34%) choosing Islamic finance due to its alignment with their value system and beliefs, followed by a similar number of people (30%) who said that providers are trustworthy and transparent.
Interestingly, the research found that consumers who are willing to make the switch to an Islamic finance provider were motivated by similar factors, regardless of their age group.
Knowledge of Islamic finance among UK consumers matches that of ethical and green finance
There remains a strong appetite for Islamic, ethical and green finance among UK consumers, as 41% of respondents had at least some awareness of Islamic finance. This closely correlates with ethical finance (38%) and green finance (37%), highlighting the strong alignment between the Shariah principles and sustainable and ethical practices.
Unsurprisingly, Muslim consumers were more likely to have at least some awareness of Islamic finance, with over three fifths (63%) stating this. However, Muslim consumers were also much more likely to be knowledgeable about green finance (51%) and ethical finance (55%) too, further highlighting the interconnectedness between these types of alternative finance products.
Knowledge gap among older generations
A finding consistent with Gatehouse Bank’s 2024 report is that those aged 45+ were much less likely to have knowledge of Islamic, ethical or green finance and the least likely to be open to switching to an Islamic finance provider. This is particularly prevalent for those aged 55+, with only just over 1 in 10 (11%) willing to make the switch. In comparison, over 6 in 10 (65%) of those aged 25-44 would be open to switching, followed closely by over 5 in 10 (55%) of those aged 18-24.
This highlights an opportunity for alternative finance providers to provide better education and provisions for older generations to ensure they are not missing out on what alternative finance providers have to offer.
Andy Homer, Chief Customer Officer at Gatehouse Bank, commented: “It is encouraging to see that UK consumers are increasingly willing to consider alternatives to conventional banking and are placing greater importance on choosing financial providers that align with their personal values.
“As the Islamic finance sector continues to grow, both in the UK and around the world, consumers are benefiting from greater choice and accessibility. At Gatehouse Bank, we welcome this and are proud to play our part by offering transparent, ethical products that are open to everyone, regardless of their religious background.”
*Research was commissioned by Gatehouse Bank and carried out by Censuswide. The survey anonymously surveyed 2,001 UK respondents, aged 18+ living in the UK between 28 September – 2 October 2026. Comparable services were defined as the selection of products, online services, customer support, pricing and ease of access.

content: New research by Gatehouse Bank reveals that half of UK consumers are willing to switch from conventional banking to Islamic finance if services are comparable. The study highlights strong consumer demand driven by values alignment and transparency, particularly among younger generations. The Islamic finance sector continues to see significant global growth and increasing popularity across the UK.

title: Zilch Reports $300M Annual Run Rate Off the Back of Strong FY26 Results
summary:
Zilch, the consumer payments app, has reached a $300m annual run rate and delivered two consecutive quarters of adjusted profit before tax in FY27 building on strong FY26 results announced today.
The results illustrate a year of strategic investments into the business with Zilch growing revenue 36% to £147.5m and GMV 28% to £2.4bn, while strengthening its products, technology, regulatory capabilities and brand. These investments laid the foundations for the acceleration now being seen in FY27, as the business delivers stronger revenue growth and improving underlying profitability.
Strong financial performance and growing customer engagement
Zilch delivered another year of strong financial performance in FY26, with gross profit increasing 24% to £65.6m and its revenue take rate rising from 5.98% to 6.34%, reflecting improved monetisation across the platform. Credit revenue grew 47% to £108.4m, while feature and advertising revenue increased 120% and 12% respectively, highlighting the growing contribution of additional revenue streams.
This performance was supported by continued growth in Zilch’s customer base and engagement. Yearly active users increased 21% to 970,000, while average annual spend per active customer rose 6% to £2,500. With customers making an average of 56 purchases a year, Zilch is becoming increasingly embedded in everyday spending, providing a strong foundation for continued growth.
A foundational year of strategic investment
Alongside its financial performance, FY26 was a year of deliberate investment as Zilch strengthened its products, technology and infrastructure to support its next phase of growth.
Zilch expanded its consumer proposition through new products and services, including physical cards, more flexible payment options and membership tiers, giving customers greater choice and flexibility. For merchants, the continued development of Intelligent Commerce, which uses data and AI to help brands reach customers and measure sales outcomes, further strengthened Zilch’s ambition to re-engineer the relationship between consumers and retailers.
The business also strengthened its financial and regulatory capabilities, increasing its securitisation facility to £200m, led by Deutsche Bank and supported by two of the world’s largest credit funds, providing capacity for approximately £4bn in annual GMV. Zilch ended FY26 with £106.5m in cash and secured its own FCA payments licence and Visa Principal Membership, strengthening its payments infrastructure and operational capabilities.
Together with its proposed acquisition of Fjord Bank, subject to regulatory approval, these developments have positioned Zilch to scale its operations, broaden its offering and pursue opportunities for international expansion.
Further investment to support the next phase of growth 
With the investments and strategic progress made during FY26 already translating into stronger financial performance in FY27, Zilch is continuing to invest in its UK presence and long-term growth. The company recently announced a £77m investment over ten years in a new London headquarters, which it will relocate to in 2027, providing additional capacity for its expanding workforce. Alongside its partnership with Arsenal Football Club, this reinforces Zilch’s commitment to the UK and its ambitions for the next phase of the business.

Philip Belamant, CEO and Co-Founder of Zilch, said:
“FY26 was a foundational year for Zilch. We delivered strong financial growth while making deliberate investments in our products, technology and infrastructure to strengthen the business and position ourselves for the next phase of expansion.
“We’re confident in the strength and profitability of our business model, and we’re now seeing the results of those investments. Reaching a $300m annual run rate and delivering two consecutive quarters of adjusted profit before tax demonstrates how the foundations we built during FY26 are translating into accelerated growth and stronger financial performance.
“Our ambition has always been to fundamentally change the relationship between consumers and brands, creating a more rewarding and transparent way for people to pay while delivering greater value for merchants. With a stronger platform, an expanding proposition and growing customer engagement, we’re already successfully building on this momentum.”

title: Amazon Seller Wallet GBP Launches, Giving Sellers in the UK Store More Control Over Their Money
summary:
Amazon today announced the launch of Amazon Seller Wallet GBP, giving eligible sellers a simpler way to manage proceeds earned through Amazon.co.uk.
Available directly within Seller Central, Seller Wallet GBP allows sellers based in the UK or overseas to hold funds in pounds sterling, pay UK suppliers directly and transfer money quickly to a UK bank account. GBP transfers to UK bank accounts are fast and free, giving sellers simpler access to funds for domestic business needs.
For sellers based outside of the UK, Seller Wallet GBP provides additional benefits when it comes to converting proceeds and managing their cashflow, enabling sellers to retain proceeds in GBP to pay UK suppliers or convert and send funds internationally in more than 20 currencies.
“Selling in the UK and internationally creates exciting growth opportunities, but it can also add complexity to everyday financial operations,” said Manasi Kudtarkar, General Manager of Amazon Seller Wallet. “With Seller Wallet GBP, we are giving sellers more choice and control over how they manage their UK proceeds, all from the same place they manage their business on Amazon.”
Key benefits for sellers:
Manage funds within Seller Central: Hold GBP proceeds earned through Amazon.co.uk, view balances, initiate transfers, and track the movement of funds alongside other business activities on Amazon.
Flexible transfer options: Make a one-time transfer or set up recurring schedules to send a fixed amount to your bank account weekly, every two weeks, or monthly.
See the full cost before transferring internationally: Review the exchange rate and total cost before confirming a transfer. A volume-based fee applies to international transfers and decreases as a seller's business with Amazon grows, with competitive exchange rates and no hidden markups or additional costs.
Simplify reporting and reconciliation: Access statements and transfer history within Seller Central to support cash-flow management, tax preparation, and account reconciliation.
The Seller Wallet experiences for GBP, EUR and USD are all separate and eligible sellers can enrol directly through Seller Central in a few clicks at no cost. Sellers operating in UK and EU stores can sign up for both GBP and EUR wallets at the same time using a streamlined process, while maintaining separate balances for each currency.
Seller Wallet first launched globally for the U.S. store in 2022, allowing sellers to manage and convert USD into more than 20 currencies in one place, before expanding in 2025 to seven European stores for global sellers to consolidate and manage EUR proceeds.

content: Amazon has launched Amazon Seller Wallet GBP, enabling eligible sellers on Amazon.co.uk to hold, manage, and transfer British pounds directly within Seller Central. The tool allows UK and international sellers to pay suppliers, make fast bank transfers, and convert funds into over 20 currencies. Designed to simplify financial operations, the wallet is free to enroll in and expands Amazon Seller Wallet's existing global currency offerings.
